questions.text: Is this post (including any text in attached images) about United States politics, public policy, or culture war, written as if the author lives in the US? Examples: Democrats or Republicans, US politicians, the minimum wage, prices, rent, or wages in dollars or in US cities, the cost of living, US healthcare or insurance, taxes, student loans, guns, immigration, or 'in this country' complaints about America. Answer no for investing, stocks, markets, or opinions about companies and their products, for posts that are not about the US, and for neutral news reports.

Is the main subject of this post (including any text in attached images) capitalism vs socialism, billionaires or "eat the rich", or the rich vs the working class, and is it a sweeping slogan or bold claim designed to farm replies rather than a specific argument? Answer no when the post is mainly about something else (technology, AI, science, sports, a product, war, geopolitics, or countries and their relations, including memes about nations), including predictions that technology will make people richer, and for specific, substantive arguments, news, or personal anecdotes.

Is the author of this post (including any text in attached images) against modern technology, with a sweeping slogan or bold claim that people don't want it or that it is ruining things (for example "nobody wants self-driving cars", "nobody asked for AI", "smartphones ruined everything", "stop building data centers")? Answer no if the author is in favor of technology or progress, including when they insult or mock the people who oppose it. Answer no for specific, substantive arguments, news, or personal anecdotes.

stance.text: A reply-quote: the author wrote the first part, quoting the post after [Quoted post]. Does the author side with the quoted post, wanting readers to agree with it? Answer no if the author is mocking it, arguing against it, correcting it, warning people about it, or commenting on something else.
